title: Largest of Three Numbers
problem_statement: Read three integers and print the largest value. The values may be equal or negative. Solve this using comparisons rather than Python's built-in `max` function or sorting the inputs. Track the largest value seen so far and compare each remaining value against it. In a brief code comment, state the invariant your comparisons maintain: after processing some inputs, the tracked value is the largest among those processed.
input_format: Three lines. Each line contains one integer.
output_format: Print the largest of the three input integers as one integer, with no extra text.
starter_code:
def main():
    first = int(input())
    second = int(input())
    third = int(input())

    # TODO: Add a brief comment stating the invariant your comparisons maintain.
    # TODO: Choose a value to track as the largest seen so far.
    largest = first

    # TODO: Compare the other two values with largest and update it when needed.

    print(largest)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

public_samples.explanation: -3 is the greatest value, even though all three values are negative.
All values are equal, so their largest value is 6.
The middle value is at the upper constraint boundary and is greater than the other two.
The largest value appears twice; either occurrence gives the same answer.

hints: You need one value that represents the best candidate found so far.
Start by treating the first input as the current largest. Check each other input against it.
For each remaining number, replace the current largest only when that number is greater. After both comparisons, print the tracked value.
common_beginner_mistakes: Comparing only the first and second inputs and forgetting to compare the third.
Initializing the largest value to 0, which fails when all three inputs are negative.
Updating the tracked largest value in only one of the needed comparisons.
Using `>=` incorrectly in a way that assigns a smaller value, or reversing the comparison operands.
Assuming the inputs arrive in sorted order.
Failing to test equal values, even though equality must still produce the correct largest value.
completion_criteria: Reads exactly three integers, one per line.
Uses comparisons, not `max` or sorting, and includes a brief comment explaining the invariant that the tracked value is largest among the inputs processed so far.
Handles any input order, negative numbers, ties, all-equal values, and the stated boundary values.
Passes all public samples and separately maintained private tests.
